page: OVHcloud r3-512-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz using AMD EPYC processors. Memory allocation is massive, offering 512.0 GB of system RAM at an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 20 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. No hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this instance type.

Benchmark data shows exceptionally strong parallel computing and memory performance. Multi-core compute tests via stress-ng place the instance in the top 10% with a score of 194,787.36, complemented by top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 764.93 GB/sec. Cached small-block memory reads attain 8,253.44 GB/sec, while uncached write operations reach 99.66 GB/sec. Real-world service metrics are consistent with this profile, capturing 124.5 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.81 GB/sec in static web throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs center around storage limitations and vector extensions. While the server provides substantial RAM and 64 non-hyperthreaded cores, the local NVMe capacity is constrained to 50 GB, requiring external storage architectures for large persistent footprints. The processor lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions, resulting in moderate token generation throughput during LLM inference (19.6 tokens/sec on 7B models), despite solid prompt processing speeds of 212.35 tokens/sec.

The configuration presents high cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing dedicated compute cores and high RAM density over large local storage arrays. It is an optimal platform for in-memory data structures, caching tiers like Redis, multi-threaded batch decompression, memory-bound enterprise applications, and compute-intensive workloads that require non-oversubscribed cores.
